newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia delays launch of two satellites.
newsitem.headline: Russia delays launch of two satellites.

text.p: Russia has postponed the launch of two commercial satellites planned this month for foreign clients until February or March, Itar-Tass news agency said on Thursday.

Sergei Zhiltsov, a spokesman for the Khrunichev State Space Centre, told Tass the delays in launching the Tempo and Iridium satellites had been requested by the foreign clients for "organisational reasons".
He did not identify the clients and did not say precisely when the launches had originally been scheduled.
Zhiltsov said the decision was not connected with the failure last month of a probe which crashed back to earth soon after blasting off on a $300-million mission to Mars.
The Mars probe was being lifted into space by the same type of high-powered Proton booster rocket which will eventually carry the two commercial satellites into space.

Tass said the satellite launches would have been postponed anyway because the use of Proton rockets, which are made at the Khrunichev centre, has been banned until a state commission ends an investigation into the failure of the Mars mission.
The Khrunichev centre has sent two satellites into space this year on behalf of foreign clients and plans to send up about 20 satellites by the year 2000.
This is planned as a major source of funding for the cash-strapped Russian space progamme.
